etymologies.etymologyHTML: From micro- +‎ -phone.

definitions.definition: A device (transducer) used to convert sound waves into a varying electric current; normally fed into an amplifier and either recorded or transmitted over radio.

quote.citation: 1965, Charles McDowell, Campaign Fever: The National Folk Festival, from New Hampshire to November, 1964, Morrow, page 11:
quote.text: Behind the tangled garden of microphones that had sprouted on the lectern, Goldwater spoke softly and casually about his family.

quote.citation: 1994, High Definition Television: An Annotated Multidisciplinary Bibliography, 1981-1992‎[1], page 112:
quote.text: It rained hard through most of Roosevelt's Second Inaugural. Audio tape recordings of the speech feature the tattoo of the rain on Roosevelt's microphone […]

definitions.definition: (transitive) To put one or more microphones on or in.
